item.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation finally gets a 2027 release date, as Final Fantasy Resonance gets a surprise demo
item.dc:creator: Dom Peppiatt
item.description:
We already knew that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation was going to launch sometime in 'spring 2027', but today director Naoki Hamaguchi took to Sony's State of Play livestream to inform us all that the game has a locked-in release date: 8th April, 2027. It'll launch worldwide, and on all platforms - that's PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X/S, and PC - at the same time (the first game in the series to do so).
In case you're unaware, the game is the final part of a trilogy that began with Final Fantasy 7 Remake and tells the story of the original FF7 in three parts. This closing chapter sees Cloud finally catch up to Sephiroth as the heroic gang tries to prevent the almighty meteor from colliding with the planet. To make matters worse, the existential threat to all life on the continent has also awoken planetary defense mechanisms known as Weapons which, in defending the planet at all costs, may also pose a risk to humanity. D'oh.
The State of Play trailer showed off new gameplay footage, showing us how Cid's airship - the Highwind - can be used to travel to the regions of the world. This will be the biggest game in the trilogy, by far, including all the locations we've seen in the other games, plus some new original areas, too. It's very much 'the final disc' of the original FF7, if you ask me, and has been scaled appropriately. I recently had a big chat with Hamaguchi, and was taken aback by his humbleness and vision for the trilogy. If you're excited about what t he game has to offer, I encourage you to give the feature a read.
Elsewhere, Square Enix has announced a playable demo for its upcoming HD-2D RPG, Final Fantasy Resonance. Downloadable today (and weighing in at about 5GB), the demo lets you try out the entire first chapter of the game. This is about three to five hours of game. And - as Square Enix has got in the habit of doing - it will let you import any save data to the full game when it launches next month.
Though this was announced in a PS5 stream, the demo is also available on Switch, Switch 2 and Xbox. I got to play a different bit of the game at Gamescom, and it left me really impressed - take a look at my Final Fantasy Resonance preview if you want to know why this was, probably, my game of the show.

item.title: A Lego replica of the original PlayStation will be available next month
item.dc:creator: Connor Makar
item.description:
A Lego replica of the original Playstation was just revealed at the Sony State of Play, and it'll be available to order starting next month.
At 1:1 scale and featuring 1,911 individual pieces, this build will feature an openable disc tray, pressable buttons, and various easter eggs including lovely little Ape Escape and Gran Turismo dioramas. It also comes with a lego PlayStation 1 controller which you can build alongside the brick console for a fancy collectors piece.
Those Dioramas can be pulled out of the console and displayed separately for those who'd prefer to do so. It's a nice touch, especially given we've not seen Ape Escape or Gran Turismo get much love in recent years. There are apparently, according to the PlayStation Blog accompanying this reveal, other hidden secrets within this set worth looking out for.
This collaboration was announced as part of the 30th anniversary celebration of PlayStation, and it'll be available to buy via Playstation Direct on the 1st October for those in the U.S, U.K, France, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, and Portugal. It'll also be available through Lego Insiders early access and in all Lego stores starting on the 4th October.
As for its price, this Lego replica will retail for £139.99 in the UK / €159.99 in Europe / $179.99 (including tax) in the US.
Sony is far from the only gaming giant to partner with Lego. Nintendo has collaborated for Lego sets for a few years now, with a Donkey Kong set seemingly leaked recently. Microsoft, on the other hand, has instead recently partnered with Mattel Brick Shop for an original Xbox build, which while a little "we have Lego at home", does look rather snazzy.
This isn't the only collectors item announced during the State of Play. Limited edition Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 controllers were also revealed, and will be available to order later this month.

item.title: GTA 6 is getting two limited edition dualsense PS5 controllers
item.dc:creator: Connor Makar
item.description:
Two limited Edition Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 Dualsense controllers were just revealed during the Sony State of Play livestream.
The controllers, one black and the other white, both feature the palm tree leaf detailing and a colour-shifting finish, as well as the game's name on the back. There's even the roman numerals for six on the touch pad in the GTA font, with additional palm tree styling to finish the pads off.
The controllers will be available to order via PlayStation Direct on the 10th September, at 10am in each region. They'll be on sale for $84.99 USD / ¥12,480 (including tax) / €84.99 / £74.99 respectively.
There's no word on just how limited these controllers will be, but judging by how prior limited edition versions of PlayStation hardware has sold out, such as the 30th anniversary bundle, it's safe to assume these will fly off the digital shelves in a similar fashion.
This announcement comes shortly after a gigantic extended gameplay reveal of Grand Theft Auto 6 on Netflix, which proved so popular as to temporarily crash the platform, as well as gaming streaming platform Twitch where millions of spectators were tuned in to live reactions. The reveal was packed full of plenty of reveals, such as side activities players can engage with, a new wanted system, some details on the romance and bond system, and more.
